A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Cooperative Sheaf Neural Networks by the same authors. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: V2 reports original CSNN experiments on NeighborsMatch, eleven node-classification benchmarks, and the two Peptides tasks in Section 6.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds Penn94 evaluation, a learned-routing experiment, and runtime measurements in Appendices B and D.

M1.justification: The directed-graph construction, composed normalized Laplacians, CSNN update in Equation 6, conformal restriction maps, and Householder parameterization are unchanged. Expanded normalization explanations and new evaluations do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Appendix B adds Penn94 node classification and an actual four-node path experiment with distracting information at intermediate nodes. These extend coverage within the existing heterophily and selective-communication themes; the original benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: V3 substantially broadens relevant comparisons: Section 6.1 adds literature-reported BuNN results and measured orthogonal-NSD results to NeighborsMatch; Table 2 adds FSGNN, GloGNN, ACMGCN, and CO-GNN. The new Penn94 comparison also introduces WRGAT and LINKX. This fills important comparator gaps in the existing experiments.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce seconds-per-epoch timing and a three-layer noisy-path inspection using coefficient norms to assess node influence. Existing fixed splits, cleaned Squirrel/Chameleon preprocessing, Peptides parameter budget, and documented training configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B and Figure 6 add a learned-routing case study testing whether selective communication emerges with distracting node information, extending the earlier constructed example. Appendix D adds empirical runtime and parameter-efficiency analysis alongside the retained complexity calculation.

E5.justification: Table 8 newly specifies that runtime means average measurements over ten epochs. This adds a timing aggregation procedure, not evidence of additional independent training runs. Existing split and seed information and mean-plus-dispersion reporting remain unchanged; the new variance caveat is not a significance test.

E6.justification: Shared scores in Tables 1–3 and the original NeighborsMatch curve are unchanged, but v3 substantially extends the results with sheaf comparisons, four Table 2 baselines, Penn94 results, and routing/runtime measurements. Penn94 CSNN is reported as 86.00 ± 0.39. ACMGCN's added Texas score of 87.84 exceeds CSNN's retained 87.30, reducing CSNN's Table 2 mean-score wins to two of four despite the unchanged three-of-four caption.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.2 states a nonlinear sheaf-Laplacian formula with continuous edge functions and sketches an argument extending Proposition 3.1 to that setting. The existing definitions, propositions, proofs, and asymptotic complexity derivation are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The introduction and contribution list qualify the empirical superiority claim: CSNN now 'typically' outperforms prior sheaf and cooperative models instead of 'consistently' surpassing them. The central directed-sheaf, cooperative-behavior, and long-range communication contributions retain their scope.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 newly cautions that Table 2's small datasets yield high variance and potentially statistically insignificant results, replacing the previous significant-margin wording. Additional discussion interprets flexible one-/two-hop routing, selective sensitivity, and runtime through parameter counts. The conclusion's existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds Penn94 dimensions, noisy-path construction and visualization rules, measured training times, and Roman-empire parameter counts: 2,269,714 for GCN and 339,900 for CSNN. Existing hyperparameter grids, GPU/RAM disclosure, preprocessing instructions, and the future code-release promise are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds references on nonlinear sheaf diffusion, FSGNN, GloGNN, ACMGCN, and the heterophilic graph-learning handbook. Related work also clarifies that the cited quiver-Laplacian work addresses tabular feature selection without learning. The principal positioning against existing sheaf and cooperative models is retained.

P1.justification: There are localized prose refinements and expanded explanations in the background, analysis, related work, and results. Section 6.1 reorders existing discussion, and the new Additional Experiments appendix shifts the retained experiment-details and complexity appendices to C and D. The overall narrative structure remains.

P2.justification: V3 adds Figures 3 and 6 and Tables 4 and 8, expands Table 2 with comparator rows, and inserts homophily rows into Tables 1–2. Some homophily values already appeared in v2's appendix. Earlier figures are retained with renumbering and relocation; the document keeps its existing visual style with local reflow.

improvement.justification: Additional relevant baselines, Penn94 evaluation, learned-routing evidence, and runtime measurements improve empirical support, while the variance caveat makes interpretation more cautious. These gains are limited by sparse details for new experiments and reporting inconsistencies: Table 2 and Section 6.2 retain win counts of three of four and nine of eleven, although the expanded comparisons support two of four and eight of eleven.
